study.title: Psalm 101: personal integrity and fair government
study.overview: This psalm presents David's commitment to integrity before God, beginning with worship and passing into private life, friendships, the choice of officers and the purification of the community. The text shows that fidelity to the LORD is not restricted to worship, but must shape the house, administration and public life. The emphasis is not only on avoiding evil, but also in promoting an environment governed by sincerity, justice, and rejection of deception.

outline.title: Praise to God's Goodness and Judgment
outline.explanation: David opens the psalm by promising to sing about the goodness and judgment of the LORD. Worship is born from the remembrance that God acts with mercy and also with justice, and this becomes the model of the king's conduct.

outline.title: Full life in private space and rejection of evil
outline.explanation: The psalmist decides to walk on the right path, with sincerity in the heart, including inside his house. He rejects what is perverse before the eyes and commits not to welcome evil in his personal life.

outline.title: Purification of the coexistence and choice of the faithful
outline.explanation: David departs from the wicked, from the slanderer, from the arrogant and the covetous, and chooses to walk with the faithful of the earth. His leadership values people on a right path and gives preference to those who serve with fidelity.

outline.title: Exclusion of the deception and cleansing of the city of the LORD
outline.explanation: Whoever uses deception or lie will have no place stable either in his house or before his eyes. The final commitment is to remove the wicked from the earth with readiness to remove those who do wickedness from the city of the LORD.

study.context: The psalm is attributed to David and, by the notes provided, is understood as a statement linked to the beginning or exercise of his government. Matthew Henry reads him as a solemn vote in taking responsibility over the house and kingdom, useful for both public administration and domestic life. Adam Clarke also presents him as a model for a wise ruler who regulates his conduct and administration by God's conduct. Tyndale points out that the psalm expresses a commitment to the integrity and rejection of evil, applicable to personal life and possibly to the sphere of government.
study.theology: Psalm unites worship and ethics: singing about the goodness and judgment of God leads the believer to desire to reflect these attributes in the way of life. The biblical integrity here is comprehensive: it includes thoughts, eyes, home, relations, office and city. There is a leadership theology that does not separate spirituality from government; on the contrary, the ruler must promote good, protect the faithful and restrict evil. At the same time, the text recognizes the need for God's help to live with righteousness, as suggested by the psalmist's implicit dependence. In evangelical reading, this ideal points to the holiness that God requires and that the commentators see fully realized in Jesus as a perfect standard, without this annulling the believer's call to obedience.

scholarViews.insight: The psalm expresses a commitment to the integrity and rejection of evil; the idea of "my house" can refer to private life or the palace, including administrative practice.
David is seen as someone who makes a solemn vow in assuming responsibility over the house and the kingdom; the psalm serves as a model for good government and also for domestic life.
The psalm is presented as a model of wise government, in which the ruler chooses the faithful and removes from the city the wicked, the liars and the corrupt.

questions: What areas of my life are out of the sincerity pattern that the psalmist takes, especially indoors?
Do my choices of coexistence and leadership value faithful and right people, or tolerate mistakes for convenience?
How does David unite praise, justice, and discipline confront the separation between personal faith and public responsibility?
study.practice: Practice a concrete review of the week: examine what you feed with your eyes, the conversations you keep and the people you influence or choose near you. If there is a lie, defamation, greed or double standard, repent and take a practical decision of cutting and substitution: reduce access to what erodes its integrity and get closer to those who walk in righteousness. If you exercise any kind of leadership at home, church, work, or service, use this psalm as a criterion for decisions that favor truth, fidelity, and justice.
study.uncertainty: The given notes allow us to affirm that the psalm is attributed to David and read as a commitment of integrity linked to the house and the government, but do not authorize with historical certainty the exact moment in which it was composed. It is also not possible to affirm, based only on the notes, whether "my house" refers exclusively to the personal residence or the royal palace; the two readings appear as interpretive possibilities. Applications about Jesus in Tyndale should be understood as interpretive reading, not as a direct conclusion of the original text.
